searches.note: Twenty four searches of a share of twenty eight for chunk h3, none of them the author's; four left unspent. Five were restricted to a house's own domain and read through their summaries: champagne-henriot.com three times (the Enchanteleurs 2015 page and sheets, the meaning of the name, the Hemera 2013 sheet), laurent-perrier.com (the Itération 26 pages) and louis-roederer.com (the Cristal 2015 press file and the Cristal page). No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the people and their dates, the village, the kind of producer, every dated change of hands, the grapes and shares, the villages, the first vintage, vintage or multi vintage, the lees, the dosage, the bottle, the other cuvées, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries; the forty five second lines were counted inside 90 to 110 words by the lint.

tested.founded: 1812 and a cooper: Wikipedia, Vinepair and others; the founder is Alphonse Pierlot in some and André Michel Pierlot, his father, in others, so he stays described.
tested.story: The cellar master's accident of 1887 and the widow's name: Wikipedia and Vinepair. The Grand Vin Sans Sucre at the end of the nineteenth century: the Union des Maisons de Champagne. The decline between the wars told as debt and the slump had no source: replaced by the daughter who ran the house after the widow's death in 1925, as two accounts give it. The buyer of 1939 is described, her dates not found. Bernard de Nonancourt at the head from October 1948: two accounts. The Cuvée Rosé of 1968 and Ultra Brut of 1981 as the Grand Vin Sans Sucre reborn: Nicolas, Difford's Guide and the Union.
tested.cuvee: Grand Siècle released in 1959 as 1952, 1953 and 1955: The Gentleman's Journal, Elite Traveler and The Finest Bubble, beside Decanter's 1960. The number on the bottle from 2019 with Itération 24 (2007, 2006 and 2004): The Finest Bubble, K and L. Itération 26: 65, 25 and 10 parts of 2012, 2008 and 2007, 58 per cent Chardonnay, 7 grams a litre, ten years on lees: Decanter, Wine.com and the house's magazine. The same shares for Itération 25 were not searched again and are cut. Les Réserves Itération 20: 21 years under natural cork in magnum, the second after Itération 17 (1995, 1993 and 1990): Decanter and Falstaff.
tested.sites: Eight Grand Cru villages for Itération 26 by the house's magazine page, the record's eight; the house's product page gives 52 and 48 and eleven villages, so the record's source is now the magazine page and the conflict is open.
tested.table: house45 credited Bernard de Nonancourt with the Champagne with no added sugar, which the widow first made in the nineteenth century: now a revived one.
tested.cards: Three cards and three questions read; one right answer each, the wrong ones of the sheet, no length clue.
